records.name: Buryatia
records.summary:
The federal framework applies in full: transition and gender-affirming healthcare are banned, there is no discrimination protection, and the 'extremism' designation has produced 101 convictions since January 2024 (98 administrative, 3 criminal) while 'propaganda' penalties rose from 22 in 2021-2022 to 257 in 2023-2024, totalling over 63 million roubles in fines.

National support groups report emigration, asylum requests and the closure of queer spaces accelerating after the designation. The audited sources document no Buryatia-specific pattern, so national conditions govern what a visitor encounters here.

records.name: Chuvashia
records.summary:
No division-specific transgender evidence appears in the surviving sources; a visitor here stands under the national framework as it operates countrywide.

As those sources establish: same-sex activity is not criminalised, but the 2023 laws ban same-sex marriage and legal gender recognition; the 'extremism' designation has produced 101 convictions since early 2024, with 'propaganda' penalties surging to 257 in 2023-24; official asylum guidance singles out trans people, open activists and one conflict-affected region cluster for heightened risk.
